reviews.text:
I've been taking my rabbit here, and they're very kind and examine him carefully.

It's first-come, first-served, not by appointment, so it's easy to go when he's not feeling well.

There are three examination rooms, so the waiting time is short.

The receptionists and nurses are all very kind, and I feel at ease bringing him here.

I've been using this clinic for nail trimming and checkups.

The doctor was very kind and attentive, which I really appreciate.

Now, while I don't mind if the order of consultations changes, waiting over 30 minutes to pay after the consultation is unacceptable.

When I pointed out that it was far too long, the person at the cashier became sullen. It was extremely unpleasant. What's that all about? Wouldn't you feel the same way if you went out to eat and had to wait that long to pay?

While the air-conditioned waiting room is nice for people, waiting that long can make animals sick, so I would like you to take that into consideration when planning your procedures.

The doctors at the hospital were very nice.

However, seeing other patients behave like that made me feel extremely upset.

I don't want to be told "take care" with such a sullen attitude.

I've been a long-time patient at this hospital, ever since it was the previous one.

All the doctors are kind and thorough, and I feel confident entrusting my precious family to this hospital.

I'm taking my chinchilla here for checkups.
I don't specifically request a particular doctor, but it's always the same doctor who's on duty, which is reassuring (*^^*)
All the staff are very friendly, and the clinic is very clean!
Thank you for your continued support.
You can go without a reservation, the staff are very friendly, and I'm happy that they're almost always open.

I've been taking my degu to this clinic. They seem very experienced in handling small animals, and they were even able to perform an X-ray without anesthesia. There's a bit of a wait since appointments aren't required, but it's great to be able to get immediate treatment when my pet suddenly becomes ill. I also appreciate that they're open on weekends and holidays.

There are no unnecessary tests or prescriptions, and the care is accurate. This means that there is no burden on the animals, which is great.
There seem to be several doctors, as there are several examination rooms.
At another hospital, I had several tests and was prescribed medication, which cost around 20,000 yen, but I was surprised that here it was only around 5,000 yen.
The parking lot is also convenient, with space for about 5 cars.

We've been taking our rabbits to this clinic for two generations.

I'm writing this to express my gratitude, as my rabbit has recovered well after a recent examination.

I don't specifically request a particular vet, but the head veterinarian usually sees my rabbits.

I take my regular vet for checkups and nail trims, but for sudden changes in my rabbit's condition, risky symptoms, or illnesses, I always bring them here for a specialist's examination.

My first rabbit had osteosarcoma of the jaw. It was a diagnosis rather than aggressive treatment. My second rabbit had suspected gastric dilation due to chocolate ingestion and intestinal obstruction.

In every examination, the vet prioritizes the animal's well-being, providing accurate treatment and making accurate judgments to ensure their happiness and comfort. It's not about being friendly or not; as a veterinarian, their professional judgment undoubtedly exceeds expectations.

I primarily rely on this clinic for secondary care, and the consultation fee (for follow-up visits) is 800 yen, and other treatment costs are reasonable compared to other secondary care clinics.

The receptionist (who also works as a veterinary nurse) wearing glasses, after listening to my symptoms during the initial consultation, went out of her way to come outside the reception area to touch the rabbit, perform a triage, and then informed me that it didn't seem to be an emergency and that she would call me according to the number.

As this is a popular animal hospital, it wouldn't be surprising if there were inconsistencies in the quality of care due to the heavy workload, but I never experienced this during my visits.

It seems that the number of animal hospitals run by the doctor's apprentices is increasing, so I hope that high-quality exotic animal care will spread throughout the country. Thank you all for your continued support.

Please take care of yourselves, and I hope you will continue to run such a great hospital.

I've been a patient here for over 10 years.

It's a bit far from my home, but the head doctor is trustworthy, so I always go here whenever I need anything.

This is a wonderful hospital that sees exotic animals without appointments, even though there's clearly a shortage of them compared to the demand.

I've seen a few comments in reviews about the head doctor's attitude, but I disagree.

He's certainly not very talkative and doesn't have a very expressive face, but he examines animals seriously and thoroughly. He listens carefully to what my family and I have to say.

There are plenty of doctors who are good at talking, have a good personality, and are approachable, but lack skill.

I'm very grateful that my dog ​​is examined thoroughly and with practiced hands.

Because my dog ​​bites and struggles, tests that other hospitals would definitely require anesthesia for are always performed by the head doctor while he's holding her, within the day's consultation time. It's a real lifesaver.

If you clearly communicate what you're concerned about and what you want him to examine, he'll do a good job.

However, since he's human, there's always a possibility of misdiagnosis, so if I had any concerns, I would immediately seek a second opinion.

I've been going there for a while, the prices are reasonable, and I'm gradually getting to know the head doctor better. It's starting to feel that way, haha ​​(I think I'm just being overly cautious. The doctor is very kind). It's a really good hospital, so I'd like to continue going there in the future!

I think all the doctors here are very skilled.
The clinic is also clean.
The reception and payment process seems to take a little time.
It gets crowded on weekends.

I had my Toy Poodle spayed and treated for a fracture by the head veterinarian. He always considers how to minimize stress on the animal. His clear and concise explanations put me at ease.

I hope to continue using this clinic as my regular veterinarian for a long time.

All the staff are efficient and very pleasant.

I have been here several times, and although the director seems to be a well-known veterinarian, as other people have said in their reviews, he can sometimes seem arrogant, so first-time visitors who don't know about him may be shocked, so be careful.

I'm relying on you for my rabbit's checkups.
The director has examined my rabbit the past few times, but the treatment was so awful that I'm writing this review to warn other rabbit owners not to have the same experience.

--
・When I was taking my rabbit out of its cage, he grabbed me by the scruff of the neck. I was surprised because I'd never experienced this with other doctors or hospitals. My pet is very precious to me, so I was very uncomfortable when he touched me in such an unaffectionate manner. Looking back, I wish I had asked for a different doctor at this point.

・Even though it was just a checkup, he asked me if I was doing well, and when I replied that I was fine, he tried to end the examination there.

Other hospitals and doctors would check my rabbit's teeth, ears, and weight fluctuations every time, so I was surprised at how careless he was.

Rabbits' teeth continue to grow and are prone to malocclusion, so they require regular checkups.

What do they think the point of checkups is if they won't even do that voluntarily? I felt that at the very least, they should have prepared a manual or something similar to check items during checkups so that all doctors could follow the same procedures.

- The director was about to finish his consultation, so I hurriedly asked them to check the above items. They did comply, but their constant annoyance left me feeling sad.

- The treatment was so bad that I half-angrily asked the receptionist, "Is it possible to change doctors from next time onwards?" They replied, "Yes, it is," with a reluctant look, and walked away.

Even though it was clear that there had been a problem during the examination, they didn't ask for a reason or even apologize. It was terrible treatment.

- After that, I told another receptionist about the above, and they politely apologized. They also told me the days when doctors other than the director were working, so I told them I would request a different doctor in the future.
---

There are few hospitals in my neighborhood that treat exotic animals, so I will continue to use your services, but I will definitely request a different doctor in the future. This is the first time I've seen a doctor who seems to have so little love for animals, and I never want to take my beloved pet to see him again.
The response may be different for dogs or cats, but I would never recommend that anyone with a rabbit have their rabbit examined by this doctor.
This is what happened to my rabbit's face (eyes) after I took it to this hospital. You absolutely should not take your rabbit there. You will regret taking it...
I came in for a check-up for my lizard. I was really worried because I couldn't find anywhere else to take it, but it's recovered and is now healthy again. I'm truly grateful.

My rabbit's left eye was leaking tears, so I took him in for an examination.

They flushed his nasolacrimal duct and prescribed eye drops, and he was better the next day!

The diagnosis was accurate and the service was quick, which was very helpful.

I would like to use their services again in the future.

In 2024, I received care for my 8-year-old ferret when he was ill.

Towards the very end, I was so overwhelmed with grief, exhaustion from caring for him day after day, a direct trip from another emergency hospital late at night, and lack of sleep, that my mind was hazy and I don't remember much. He passed away soon after, but I do remember being told that it was his time, and that I shouldn't take him around too much or have him examined too much, which would drain his energy.

They gave me instructions on what to do if he was suffering at home.

I don't know if that was the right course of action, or if it was truly what was best for my ferret.

However, after I called the reception to inform them and express my gratitude, they sent flowers to my home.

They also have a waiting system in place to minimize stress on pets, especially in summer and winter.

They provide a buzzer that sounds when it's your turn, allowing you to wait in your car or elsewhere.

You can also check the current congestion level in real time on their website.

They also have information sheets about emergency hospitals late at night.

Seeing their compassion for animals and the practical efforts they make, I feel that they are a good doctor and hospital.

I still often reread the ferret book that the doctor supervised.
Thank you to everyone at the hospital for your help.

*Added 2025/5/29
For about a year before she passed away, amidst her daily incontinence (defecating and urinating while walking), she would often exhibit a mysterious behavior: "going to a corner, chewing her mouth, and coughing (without vomiting anything)." I had doctors at two different hospitals review the video, but both said they couldn't tell anything from that alone at the time. Looking back now, I think it was highly likely to be a premonitory reaction to epilepsy (a chewing gum seizure).

A month before she passed away, she urinated green, and three days before, she had a violent epileptic seizure, her front legs twitching violently, she stopped urinating and passed away peacefully in a state of confusion. She had some tendency towards hypoglycemia, but she wasn't a particularly strong-willed ferret. She didn't exhibit circling behavior or drooling.

I'm writing this down in the hope that it might be helpful to someone someday.

We're using their services for our iguana.

There are very few veterinarians who treat iguanas, but they are incredibly caring and attentive.

They provide meticulous care and are indispensable for our iguana.

The doctor was extremely unfriendly.
When I said thank you at the end of the examination, he only replied, "Okay."
I wish he'd go back to elementary school to learn how to greet people properly. 😂 …
They are efficient and friendly.

I brought my rabbit in for an examination on the recommendation of another clinic. I was there to discuss malocclusion, dislocated toes, cataracts, persistent tearing in the left eye, and the amount of food to give. Since my usual vet wasn't available, the head veterinarian examined him this time.

Previous visit: "I'm not sure about the dislocation. The teeth are also unclear. He seems energetic, so let's wait and see. It might be good to bring him in every week. More importantly, the X-ray shows he has a lot of fat. Let's reduce his food. If he's overweight to begin with, weight alone isn't enough; let's determine the right amount for him while monitoring his food intake and weight."

"It seems like antibiotics alone aren't enough for his eyes, right? Let's try something with ingredients that stop the inflammation. Next time, I want to thoroughly check the effect of the eye drops, so please come back within one or two weeks. If this improves, just use the eye drops when he tears. That should get him better."

This visit: (Dislocation and malocclusion not examined) "This rabbit isn't overweight. His spine is bony. But he's eating too much, so please reduce his food intake." Based on this dog's weight, the amount of food should be around... Isn't she spayed? If not, it's more likely that the uterus is swollen rather than fat. Fat can't be seen on an X-ray. Let's take an ultrasound. Huh? Her eyes? Ah, the redness might be fading. Will it completely disappear? No, it won't. It won't heal. ←? ?

I asked if different doctors give different diagnoses, but they all said in unison, "Our approach is the same." Are they told to say that? I've been trying various things by trial and error because the cause is unknown, and then they just cut me off saying it won't heal, which makes no sense. Also,

- Weren't the teeth and fingers just being monitored?

- I told the previous person that I didn't understand why she wasn't spayed.

- Since weight doesn't tell you how much food, wasn't that why you were keeping a record?

- Too much food. Her spine is bony, reduce the food. What does that mean?

- You were talking about fat even though fat can't be seen on an X-ray?

"The redness seems to be subsiding." Compared to what? Isn't that what I just said?

And so on. If I trust the head veterinarian, it means the previous vet misdiagnosed. If I trust the previous vet, it means the head veterinarian didn't look at the medical record (he was so confident that he kept all the records), which made me incredibly distrustful.

The previous vet misdiagnosed, the medical record wasn't detailed enough, and the head veterinarian doesn't even know the patient. That sums it up, doesn't it?

It seems there are no more rabbit specialists. The nearby animal hospital is much better; they stay with you during X-rays and procedures, and everything from how they pick up the rabbit to their greetings is very polite. I won't be going back. Thank you.

Thank you so much for your care with my rabbit's medical visits.
Thank you for your thorough examinations every time.

For seven years, I trusted the head doctor and specifically requested him for my appointments. However, my trust in him was completely lost after a recent examination.

A year ago, during a health checkup, when it was pointed out that my dog's heart was slightly enlarged, the doctor said, "Let's wait and see." Three months ago, an X-ray also didn't mention any heart treatment. I sought a second opinion at another hospital, where my dog ​​was diagnosed with impaired liver function due to cardiac hypertrophy.

If I had followed the doctor's advice and waited, my dog's condition might have worsened. I was shocked to learn from the second opinion that heart treatment should have started much sooner.

Doctor, why didn't you suggest heart treatment? It could have started a year ago.

My dog ​​is never coming back.

Currently, further discussions are underway in accordance with proper procedures, and I feel that the hospital's response is being given considerable consideration. Until a final decision is reached, I will temporarily withhold details of …

We had our tortoise treated here.

The doctor treated it very carefully and gently, despite the difficult …

This is an animal clinic that specializes in exotic animals.  I trust them very much and they are very helpful and kind in their treatment.  They are conservative in their treatment, in that I have never felt that they want to do a lot of …

I received excellent care for my bearded dragon's skin disease.

The medication and treatment were precise and very helpful.
